matched_pairs.a_claim_text_normalized: When evaluated on artwork datasets such as Picasso and People-Art, YOLO generalizes better than detectors trained only on natural images.
matched_pairs.b_claim_text_normalized: YOLO outperforms R-CNN and DPM when generalizing from natural images to artwork domains.

matched_pairs.a_claim_text_normalized: YOLO produces more localization errors than two-stage detectors and struggles with small objects appearing in groups.
matched_pairs.b_claim_text_normalized: YOLO struggles with small objects that appear in groups due to spatial constraints limiting nearby object predictions.

matched_pairs.a_claim_text_normalized: The base YOLO model processes images at approximately 45 frames per second on a Titan X GPU, while the Fast YOLO variant reaches around 155 FPS.
matched_pairs.b_claim_text_normalized: Fast YOLO processes images at 155 frames per second while achieving more than twice the mAP of other real-time detectors.

matched_pairs.a_claim_text_normalized: YOLO formulates object detection as a single regression problem from raw pixels to bounding box coordinates and class probabilities, using one neural network for the entire task.
matched_pairs.b_claim_text_normalized: YOLO frames object detection as a regression problem predicting bounding boxes and class probabilities from full images in a single network evaluation.

unmatched_a.a_claim_text_normalized: Detection is performed by dividing the input image into a fixed grid where each cell predicts a small number of bounding boxes with confidence scores and class probabilities.
